# Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)

## Getting Started

vLLM-Ascend now supports prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation with EP (Expert Parallelism) options. This guide takes one-by-one steps to verify these features with constrained resources.

Take the DeepSeek-r1-w8a8 model as an example, use 4 Atlas 800T A3 servers to deploy the "2P1D" architecture. Assume the IP of the prefiller server is 192.0.0.1 (prefill 1) and 192.0.0.2 (prefill 2), and the decoder servers are 192.0.0.3 (decoder 1) and 192.0.0.4 (decoder 2). On each server, use 8 NPUs and 16 chips to deploy one service instance.

## Verify Multi-Node Communication Environment

### Physical Layer Requirements

  * The physical machines must be located on the same LAN, with network connectivity.
  * All NPUs must be interconnected. On A2/A3, intra-node connectivity is via HCCS, and inter-node connectivity is via RDMA. For Atlas 850/850E/950 SuperPod (950PR/950DT), see Atlas 850/850E/950 SuperPod Communication Configuration.

### Motivation.

During Q3 2026, DeepSeek V4 Flash serving on Ascend received a set of coordinated performance and enablement improvements around Model Runner V2 (MRV2), prefill/decode (PD) disaggregation, long-context prefill, speculative decoding, and decode graph execution. The work has reached a useful end-to-end profile, but the supported configuration, validation boundary, and performance evidence are currently spread across implementation PRs, CI configuration, and local benchmark reports.

This RFC proposes making the Q3 DeepSeek V4 Flash profile an explicit, reproducible contract on `main` and in Nightly. The target model is DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 W8A8, not DeepSeek V4.1. The validated profile combines:
  * Keep token-aligned hidden states, position information, indexer state, KV cache writes, and DSpark metadata consistent across PCP ranks.
  * Preserve prefix-cache correctness and distinguish text-prefix repetition from measured token-cache hit rate.
  * Validate cold-Prefill and prefix-reuse workloads independently.

##### Quantized indexer KV

  * Maintain `--attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8` on both P and D.
  * Validate indexer key/value layout, scales, cache transfer, graph replay, and the first Decode step after PD handoff.
  * Treat P/D dtype or metadata mismatch as a startup error rather than silently falling back.

##### PD disaggregation

  * Keep Mooncake producer/consumer roles and heterogeneous P/D parallel layouts working under MRV2.
  * Validate KV registration, transfer completion, source-buffer lifetime, request cleanup, and the first token after handoff.
  * Add an optional strict audit mode or test extension for per-request PD/KV transfer evidence; the reference performance report did not perform this audit.

##### Decode graph execution

  * Keep target Decode in `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` while the DSpark draft model remains eager.
  * Validate graph capture/replay with changing batch size, padded slots, asynchronous scheduling, indexer KV INT8, and speculative metadata updates.
  * Retain an eager fallback test to separate graph-specific failures from model or connector failures.

##### MoE and scheduling

  * Preserve the validated fused-MC2 Prefill path and Decode shared-expert overlap/recompute scheduling.
  * Keep backend selection observable in startup logs.
  * Treat MegaMoE mode 2 as a separate capability and acceptance track under [RFC]: Support MegaMoE for DeepSeek V4 #17452; it must not silently replace the baseline used by this RFC.

### 5.2 PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: Mooncake.

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

  1. Prefill preemption interrupts Decode: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.
  2. Inflexible resource allocation: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

## 1 Introduction

!!! note
    
    `The "PD Separation Deployment" mentioned in this document is provided only as an example/reference design to demonstrate the basic process of deploying Prefill and Decode in separated mode. It is not recommended for use in the production environment.
    
    **For the production environment on the customer side, [MindIE Motor](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/en/mindie/latest/quickstart/docs/en/user_guide/quick_start.md) + vLLM Ascend is recommended.**
    `

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is a native multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B backbone parameters and a context length of up to one million tokens. It uses a 40-layer Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture with 20 causal-encoder layers and 20 decoder layers, activating 8B parameters per token during Prefill and 16B during Decode.

The model introduces Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2), FP4 main KV cache, SWA Bounded Replay, Single-Pass mHC, Engram conditional memory, and DSpark speculative decoding. These designs reduce the global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token and the persistent KV cache footprint to approximately one eighth of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The model accepts text and images and supports a continuously adjustable reasoning effort from 1 to 100.

This guide covers single-node, multi-node, Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregated, and KV Cache Pool deployment on A2 and A3 servers and 950DT products.

A2 and A3 support W4A8 and W8A8 weights; W4A8 is recommended for performance and used in the examples below. The 950DT examples use the official MXFP checkpoint.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is supported in vLLM Ascend v0.30.0rc1 and later. The examples below follow vLLM Ascend `main`. For source builds, use the upstream vLLM revision recorded in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit` at the selected vLLM Ascend commit.

## 2 Supported Features

Refer to the Supported Models for the complete support matrix and the Feature Guide for feature configuration.

# Dynamic Chunked Pipeline Parallel (DeepSeek-V3.1)

## Getting Started

vLLM-Ascend supports Dynamic Chunked Pipeline Parallel (CPP) for optimizing prefill performance in Pipeline Parallelism scenarios. This feature is supported starting from version `v0.19.1rc1`.

!!! important
    
    `**CPP is designed to be used on the P (Prefiller) node in Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregation deployments.** The D (Decoder) node does not require CPP configuration. By dynamically calculating the optimal chunk size based on profiling data, CPP significantly reduces Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for long sequences on P nodes.
    
    This guide demonstrates PD disaggregation deployment with DeepSeek-V3.1 on 3 Atlas 800T A3 servers (64GB × 16): one server acts as the Prefiller (P node, with CPP enabled) and two servers act as the Decoder (D nodes, without CPP, DP32 standard configuration).
    `

For configuration details, see the Feature Guide.

For design details, see the Design Document.

For complete PD disaggregation setup instructions (environment verification, Mooncake installation, proxy deployment), see:

  * PD Disaggregation Single Node (Qwen2.5-VL)
  * PD Disaggregation Multi Node (DeepSeek)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the decode node, enabling TP fine-grained splitting (`finegrained_tp_config`) for oproj/mlp — which requires `tensor_parallel_size=1`, so the node was moved from dp8/tp2 to dp16/tp1 — together with the required companions (`scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable=true`, `MultiConnector` = MooncakeHybridConnector + PreemptOffloadConnector, `max_num_seqs` lowered to 8 so the cudagraph capture bound covers the largest decode step) makes the engine produce deterministic garbage text for every request. The engines themselves start and stay perfectly healthy; nothing crashes.

### Describe the bug

Decode DP ranks progressively retain running requests while both token-generation
and request-completion counters stop advancing. The HTTP health and metrics
endpoints continue returning 200, and the router remains active. As more ranks
stop making progress, new work is routed only to the remaining healthy rank.

This was reproduced with DeepSeek-V4-Flash W8A8 MTP using Mooncake P/D
disaggregation on Ascend A3.

#### Topology

  * Prefill: 3 nodes, each DP=4 / TP=4
  * Decode: 1 node, DP=16 / TP=1 / EP enabled
